claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in college or anything like that. He finished school but he's not studying anymore.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Since Alex is 17 and not in full-time education or an approved training course, I have one more question:

Has Alex recently left education or training (within the past 20 weeks), or has he registered with a careers service, Connexions, or the Ministry of Defence for work or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he left school a while back and hasn't signed up with any careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me just confirm the key points:
- Alex is 17 years old
- He is not in full-time education or approved training
- He has not registered with a careers service or the armed services for work or training (and it has been more than 20 weeks since he left education)

Based on the UK government's Child Benefit eligibility rules, I'm afraid I have to share some disappointing news:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of the UK government's Child Benefit eligibility rules, I'm sorry to tell you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 17) - Not Eligible**

Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16. For those aged 16 or over, eligibility can continue only if the child:
- Stays in approved education or training (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar) until they turn 20, **or**
- Registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services within 20 weeks of leaving education (which allows Child Benefit to continue for a further 20 weeks)

Since Alex is 17, has left school, is not in approved education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services, he unfortunately does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

**What you could consider:**
If Alex were to return to approved full-time education or training before turning 20, you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit for him again at that point.

If you have any other questions or would like further clarification, please don't hesitate to ask.

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old, which means he is over the standard qualifying age of 16 for Child Benefit. For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can continue only if the child stays in approved education or training (until they turn 20). Alex has left school and is not in any form of approved education or training. Additionally, there is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services - however, Alex has not done this, and it has been longer than 20 weeks since he left education. Furthermore, if a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training, eligibility stops. Since Alex does not meet any of the criteria that would extend Child Benefit beyond age 16, he is not eligible.
